title: Americans retain commitment to democracy while national performance and accountability decline, producing a local-national legitimacy split
source_unit: Gallup and Charles F. Kettering Foundation, Democracy for All Project: Frustration Rises, Commitment Endures
geography: United States adults, with national and local democratic assessments and subgroup analysis in a large 2026 survey

observations.period: April 24-June 10, 2026; national democratic performance and commitment

denominator.unit: U.S. adults surveyed by Gallup for the Democracy for All Project

national_democracy_poor.unit: percent saying U.S. democracy is doing very or moderately poorly

national_democracy_well.unit: percent saying U.S. democracy is doing very or moderately well

local_democracy_well.unit: percent saying democracy in their own city or town is doing very or moderately well

local_democracy_poor.unit: percent saying democracy in their own city or town is doing very or moderately poorly

local_national_gap.value: Local democratic experience is evaluated more positively than national democratic performance.

observations.method: Gallup survey of 23,683 U.S. adults fielded April 24-June 10, 2026; reported margin of sampling error is plus or minus one percentage point at the 95 percent confidence level.
observations.uncertainty: The cross-sectional survey measures perceptions, not institutional performance audits, local policy outcomes, causal effects, or actual participation. The local-national difference may reflect scale, information, partisan evaluation, or direct experience.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults, with national and local comparisons; the public page does not provide every subgroup denominator in the summary.
observations.counterinterpretation: Local positivity can coexist with national distrust because residents know local actors more directly or use different standards; it does not prove that local institutions are more accountable or effective.

observations.period: 2026 survey; democratic trajectory and institutional accountability

democracy_weaker_50_years.unit: percent saying U.S. democracy was much or somewhat stronger 50 years ago than today

future_weaker.unit: percent expecting U.S. democracy to become much or somewhat weaker over the next 50 years

future_stronger.unit: percent expecting U.S. democracy to become much or somewhat stronger over the next 50 years

leaders_held_accountable.unit: percent trusting that political leaders will be held accountable to the nation's laws and Constitution

trajectory_mechanism.value: Democratic commitment persists alongside pessimistic historical and future trajectory judgments and weak confidence in constitutional accountability.

observations.method: Descriptive survey estimates from the Democracy for All Project summary.
observations.uncertainty: Expectations and retrospective comparisons are not forecasts or historical institutional measures; trust in accountability does not identify which actors, cases, or mechanisms drive the judgment.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults across political and demographic groups; detailed subgroup patterns require the full report or dataset.
observations.counterinterpretation: Pessimistic trajectory judgments may coexist with democratic commitment because people distinguish democratic ideals from current officeholders or institutional performance.

rule_of_law_weaker.unit: percent saying the rule of law is weaker than 10 years ago, compared with 14 percent saying stronger

executive_power_too_high.unit: percent saying the executive branch has too much power

judicial_power_too_high.unit: percent saying the judicial branch has too much power

legislative_power_too_high.unit: percent saying the legislative branch has too much power

equal_treatment_poor.unit: percent rating how well all people are treated equally under the law as very or moderately poorly, up from 55 percent

observations.method: Large-sample Gallup/Kettering survey summary of institutional and rule-of-law perceptions.
observations.uncertainty: These are public judgments, not constitutional adjudications or branch-level power measurements; perceptions can be partisan, issue-specific, and event-sensitive.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults; summary page does not provide full subgroup denominators for each institutional measure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Concern about executive power can reflect checks-and-balances preferences rather than generalized democratic collapse; equal-treatment ratings may be driven by salient cases or media environments.

observations.period: 2026 report; local trust as a democratic buffer

local_trust_mechanism.value: Americans who trust local leaders and neighbors view democracy more positively at both local and national levels.

inclusion_fairness_opportunity.value: The project frames democratic experience through inclusion, fairness, opportunity, ordinary people's ability to create positive change, and sensitivity of elected leaders to local needs.

participation_boundary.value: The summary identifies commitment and participation as necessary to democratic realization but does not report observed participation, organized action, policy influence, or remedy.

observations.method: Review of the Gallup/Kettering project description and 2026 report summary; association is retained separately from causal or behavioral evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not establish whether local trust causes better national democratic evaluations, whether neighbors and leaders are trusted for the same reasons, or which interventions build trust.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults with variation in local experience, place, political identity, and social connection; detailed estimates require the full data release.
observations.counterinterpretation: People who are generally more trusting may rate both local and national democracy more positively, producing a common-attitude association rather than a local institutional buffer.

related_sources.claim: Gallup and the Kettering Foundation's September 2026 Democracy for All publication reports the survey sample, national/local democratic evaluations, institutional accountability judgments, and local-trust framing.
The Kettering Foundation context for the Democracy for All project emphasizes citizens' experience, inclusion, fairness, opportunity, and democratic participation.

boundary: This record adds a local-national democratic-legitimacy route: commitment to democratic ideals can coexist with declining national performance judgments, weak accountability confidence, rule-of-law concern, and stronger local evaluations. It does not establish institutional failure, causal local buffering, actual participation, policy influence, or durable democratic recovery.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Gallup Democracy for All publication page was reviewed for the 2026 sample and field dates, national and local performance assessments, trajectory judgments, accountability, branch-power, equal-treatment, and local-trust findings.
